historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah The name Hamd carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Hamd (praise) is mentioned in the Quran as a name of Allah and also as a word for praise and thanks. It is said that the Prophet Muhammad (p.b.u.h.) himself used to call Allah by the name Hamd. Ibn Abbas (r.a.) reported that the Prophet (p.b.u.h.) said, 'Allah is Hamd (praise), and Hamd is Allah.'

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Al-Qayyim's I'lam Al-Mu'minin The name Hamd carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Al-Qayyim wrote in his book 'I'lam Al-Mu'minin' that the origin of the name Hamd is from the Arabic word 'Hamdah' which means 'to praise' or 'to extol'. The Prophet Muhammad (p.b.u.h.) used to call Allah by this name and teach his companions to do the same. It is also mentioned in the Quran that Allah is the One who is praised and glorified (Al-Muddaththir:12).
